records.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering: Literature Review, Vision, and the Road Ahead
records.rationale: Abstract is truncated but the title is unambiguous: a dedicated literature review of LLM-based MAS scoped to software engineering with an explicit forward-looking research agenda, which covers the review scope, open challenges, and future-work component of RQ1.

records.title: AgentNet: Decentralized Evolutionary Coordination for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: The snippet confirms a named decentralized coordination architecture benchmarked against both single-agent and centralized multi-agent baselines, which is relevant to RQ2, but no software engineering task or failure-mode measurement is visible, so it contributes a coordination mechanism rather than direct SE evidence.

records.title: Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: Failure attribution across collaborating specialized agents is precisely the RQ3 target, and the snippet notes that tighter coordination introduces conflicts a single agent never encounters, giving a direct account of coordination-induced failure modes.

records.title: Rethinking software engineering for agentic ai systems
records.rationale: Combines systematic verification and multi-agent orchestration within an SE framing, and the snippet reports the conditional finding that no single agent configuration was universally optimal, which is the exact contingency RQ2 asks about.

records.title: AgentForge: Execution-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Autonomous Software Engineering
records.rationale: Reports 40.0% resolution on SWE-Bench Lite with a 26-28 point margin over single-agent baselines plus ablations isolating execution feedback from role decomposition, supplying quantified RQ2 evidence and an explicit verification-by-sandboxed-execution mechanism for RQ3.

records.title: Llm-based agentic systems for software engineering: Challenges and opportunities
records.rationale: SE-scoped survey that contrasts single-agent systems such as AUTOFL against multi-agent designs and enumerates open challenges, matching the comparative-performance and future-work strands of RQ1.

records.title: Multi-agent collaboration mechanisms: A survey of llms
records.rationale: Provides a general taxonomy of LLM collaboration mechanisms that is useful vocabulary for classifying coordination structures in RQ3, but it is domain-agnostic and the snippet shows no software engineering application or measured failure analysis.

records.title: Understanding multi-agent LLM frameworks: A unified benchmark and experimental analysis
records.rationale: Holds the underlying model fixed while systematically comparing single-agent against multi-agent settings across frameworks, which is the cleanest available controlled design for isolating the orchestration effect asked about in RQ2.

records.title: The Rise of Agentic Testing: Multi-Agent Systems for Robust Software Quality Assurance
records.rationale: Positions multi-agent testing explicitly against the limitations of single-agent automation and reports comparative coverage and test-quality results against static LLM baselines, giving RQ2 evidence inside the SE testing and QA activity.

records.title: Developing LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering: A Mixed-Method Experience Report
records.rationale: The empirical comparison is across MAS frameworks on a README summarization task rather than multi-agent versus single-agent, but the null ROUGE result, the missing agent telemetry finding, and the coordination-rule and role-design difficulties are combinable inputs for the verification and observability discussion.

records.title: CAPRA: Scaling Feedback on Software Architecture Deliverables with a Multi-Agent LLM System
records.rationale: Applies specialized agents to architecture-deliverable review and contributes concrete hallucination-control machinery (deterministic Evidence Anchoring plus a cross-verifying ConsistencyManager agent) plus an eight-criterion evaluation taxonomy, but it reports no single-agent comparison.

records.title: MOSAIC: A Pattern Catalog and Formal Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Frames the shift from single-agent code generation to specialized-agent orchestration in SE and formalizes it as a pattern catalog benchmarked against three established frameworks, directly serving the orchestration-conditions question in RQ2.

records.title: Emergent Intelligence in Multi-Agent and LLM Systems: A Survey and Perspective Toward Autonomous, Collaborative, and Generalizable AI
records.rationale: A broad perspective piece aimed at emergent and generalizable AI rather than software engineering, with only a passing note that conventional schemes assume fixed or single agents, so it sets background framing without supplying comparative or failure-mode evidence.

records.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Orchestration: A Survey of Frameworks, Communication Protocols, and Emerging Patterns
records.rationale: Its survey of inter-agent communication protocols and emerging orchestration patterns supplies a coordination-mechanism vocabulary for RQ3, but the snippet indicates it deliberately treats single-agent LLM surveys only peripherally and reports no SE-task outcomes.

records.title: From llms to llm-based agents for software engineering: A survey of current, challenges and future
records.rationale: An SE-scoped survey that explicitly organizes the field into single-agent and multi-agent branches and offers a comparative overview together with limitations, covering the comparative-performance and future-work parts of RQ1 from a 2024 baseline.

records.title: Observability and Fault Injection for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Only bibliographic metadata is present, but fault injection plus observability for LLM MAS at ICST is the rare paper that both induces and instruments coordination failures, which is exactly the how-are-they-measured half of RQ3.

records.title: A Systematic Survey of LLM-Based Agentic AI Frameworks for Multi-Agent Coordination and Interoperability
records.rationale: Surveys coordination and interoperability across agentic frameworks and includes a comparative study of representative systems, which informs RQ3 coordination structures, but the snippet argues for multi-agent architectures rather than testing when they win.

records.title: Designing LLM-based multi-agent systems for software engineering tasks: Quality attributes, design patterns and rationale
records.rationale: Studies the transition from single-agent to a four-specialized-agent design for SE tasks using Open Coding and Constant Comparison, tying design patterns to quality attributes and documented rationale, which addresses both the conditions in RQ2 and design-level reliability concerns.

records.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Code Generation: A Multi-Vocal Literature Review
records.rationale: A multi-vocal review focused on the specific claim that multiple agents beat single-agent approaches for code generation, giving both an SE-task synthesis for RQ1 and a grey-literature evidence base that a purely academic search would miss.

records.title: Multi-Agent Systems and Their Evolution: A Comparative Survey
records.rationale: Traces MAS lineage from classical coordination through LLM systems such as MetaGPT, so it is genealogical background rather than an SE-scoped comparison, and its single-agent remarks are motivational rather than empirical.

records.title: Automated Black-Box Testing: A Comparative Study of LLM Agent Architectures and Prompt Engineering
records.rationale: No abstract was retrieved, but a comparative study of LLM agent architectures for black-box testing is a direct architecture-versus-architecture experiment in an SE activity, and it additionally isolates prompt engineering as a confound for RQ2.

records.title: Automated Summarization of Software Documents: An LLM-based Multi-Agent Approach
records.rationale: Metagente contributes a named Teacher-Student multi-agent architecture evaluated on real-world software documentation and requirements artifacts, but the reported baselines are not characterized as single-agent configurations, so it supplies an architecture pattern rather than RQ2 comparative evidence.

records.title: A Survey on Reliability, Transparency, Accountability, and Fairness in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through the Responsibility Lens
records.rationale: Reliability is only one of four responsible-AI properties examined and the SE mention is incidental, so the paper supplies an auditing and accountability lens plus reliability vocabulary for RQ3 rather than measured failure modes or performance comparisons.

records.title: From fragmentation to systematic design: Architecting llm-based multi-agent systems
records.rationale: Contributes architectural guidance on cross-agent memory that extends beyond single-agent state and on shared-versus-competing specialized agent selection, which is a design-level input to RQ2 conditions without itself reporting an SE benchmark.

records.title: Engineering LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems: A Taxonomy of Emerging Frameworks
records.rationale: Metadata only, but an IEEE Software taxonomy of emerging LLM MAS frameworks provides a practitioner-facing classification scheme for organizing the architecture landscape, which supports synthesis without answering a research question itself.

records.title: SPEAR: An Engineering Case Study of Multi-Agent Coordination for Smart Contract Auditing
records.rationale: Empirically compares a specialized multi-agent design against centralized and pipeline alternatives under controlled failure scenarios while measuring coordination, recovery behavior, and resource use, hitting RQ2 and RQ3 simultaneously in an SE verification and security workflow.

records.title: Context Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Code Assistants Using Elicit, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and Claude Code
records.rationale: Reports higher single-shot success and better project-context adherence than baseline single-agent approaches on a real Next.js repository, and attributes the gain jointly to context injection and agent role decomposition, which is the confound RQ2 needs disentangled.

records.title: Facilitating Trustworthy Human-Agent Collaboration in LLM-based Multi-Agent System oriented Software Engineering
records.rationale: Asserts rather than demonstrates that MAS outperform singular agents in SE, and the truncated abstract points to a trust and human-oversight vision contribution, so it informs the verification and accountability discussion without supplying comparative results.

records.title: A comprehensive survey on benchmarks and solutions in software engineering of llm-empowered agentic system
records.rationale: Catalogs the benchmarks used to evaluate LLM agentic systems in SE alongside the increasingly apparent limitations of single-agent systems, which directly serves the measurement half of RQ3 and anchors the evaluation instruments used across the corpus.

records.title: Risk analysis techniques for governed LLM-based multi-agent systems
records.rationale: Offers risk-analysis techniques and critique-comparison metrics for interacting specialized agents, and notes that multi-agent structure can sometimes mitigate single-agent failures, but the governance and business-unit framing keeps it outside direct SE evidence.

records.title: Traceability and Accountability in Role-Specialized Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
records.rationale: Metadata only, yet the title targets role-specialized pipelines specifically on traceability and accountability, which is the attribution mechanism RQ3 requires for locating coordination failures, and its six citations suggest it is already an anchor for this subtopic.

records.title: Beyond More Agents: A Survey of Collaboration Mechanisms in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.rationale: Explicitly critiques prior surveys for reporting system performance without comparing collaboration mechanisms, and frames the analysis around when a single frontier agent suffices versus when work should be split across specialized agents, which is the RQ2 framing stated almost verbatim.

records.title: An empirical comparison of multi-agent LLM architectural patterns for automated unit test generation
records.rationale: Promoted well above its rank 53 position because it runs a controlled experiment comparing three patterns including an explicit Single-Agent Baseline on unit test generation, and reports a decomposition penalty where splitting into specialized workers eliminates environmental context.
